hypothesis: Within a state, +10 pp Medicare Advantage participation is associated with a higher FFS cardiac imaging rate per 1,000 FFS beneficiaries (IRR > 1), because people who stay in FFS cost more.
data: GV PUF (already loaded): MA_PRTCPTN_RATE, BENES_OM_CNT, BENE_DUAL_PCT; state + year
design: State-year Poisson QMLE with state and year FE, 2018–2023, plus an analytic bias bound on published changes
threat: Expected effect is small (~1–2.5% over 2018–2023), so the panel may be underpowered; MA spillover pulls the other way

hypothesis: After the Oct 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain guideline, the CTA trend steepened (+) and the SPECT trend fell further (−), with echo unchanged (negative control).
data: Already in hand: claims by HCPCS, state, year
design: Comparative interrupted time series by state-year; 2020 dropped or modelled; test a change in slope, not level
threat: COVID recovery happens at the same time; only two post-guideline years

hypothesis: Cardiologists who gain a hospital affiliation or join a top-quartile-size group shift echo and SPECT from office to facility billing (+), with no change in total volume.
data: CMS Doctors & Clinicians file (archived releases): Org_PAC_ID, num_org_mem, hosp_afl_1–5; NPI
design: NPI-year staggered difference-in-differences on the switch year
threat: Snapshots are not a clean panel; acquisition changes billing without changing where care happens

hypothesis: Physicians who first receive industry payments tied to a product (FFR-CT, PET tracer) bill more of the matching modality afterwards (+), with no change for unrelated products.
data: CMS Open Payments general payments: recipient NPI (2021+), product name; NPI + year
design: NPI-year event study on first payment; unrelated-product payments as negative control
threat: Reverse causation (manufacturers target high-volume readers); suppression of low-volume rows

hypothesis: Counties with no cardiologist and low CT supply have a lower CTA-to-SPECT ratio than metro counties (−), with a wider rural gap for CTA, PET and MRI than for echo.
data: HRSA Area Health Resources File: cardiologist counts, CT supply; county FIPS
design: County cross-section, repeated by year, age/sex standardized
threat: Provider-file suppression (< 11 beneficiaries) and provider-address geography push rural rates toward zero

hypothesis: HRRs with higher standardized SPECT + CTA rates have no lower 30-day AMI/HF mortality (slope ≈ 0).
data: Dartmouth ZIP→HRR crosswalk (2019); Care Compare MORT_30_AMI/HF via hospital CCN
design: HRR-year ecological analysis; descriptive, cannot support a causal claim
threat: Imaging located by provider address, not patient; confounding by indication

hypothesis: The CY2025 hospital-outpatient payment rise for CTA (75574) increased facility CTA relative to office CTA and facility SPECT (+).
data: OPPS Addendum B by HCPCS + year (payment size unverified); needs the 2025 provider file
threat: Untestable in the 2018–2023 window; the provider file never shows the facility payment
status: candidate (post hoc, no plan; data not yet released)
